Suddenly, it caught attention and people started drawing fanarts, soon it exploded into popularity, it started selling merch like crazy and the DVDs went out of stock, it topped charts even against famous franchises, it sparked great interest at Japanese zoos basically reviving them, it got collaborations with other companies and advertisers. It was a real underdog story showing the power of passion, the director behind it(Tatsuki) was extremely surprised and took it very personally, he had acquired a massive following of grateful fans. As a big "thank you" to all the fans that support him, he made another bonus episode entirely funded by himself, and posted it on Twitter for free.

Of course such unexpected success was also a golden piggy bank for the corporates behind him. However, the production and publishing company KADOKAWA didn't take that "thank you" lightly and accused the director of making unauthorized content abusing copyright agreements, which then resulted in firing him - the guy who brought them so much money and who basically organized and created the whole thing.

It was a big example of incompetent corporate greed fucking everyone over and ripping the soul of a very special and successful project, they even announced a second season but with an entirely different team it wouldn't have the same charm and the people boycotted them for trying to ride on stolen success, canceling subscriptions of their premium video service.
